# Decision history — templartorrent

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## templartorrent.decision.fork-rbit-for-native-gate

### Revision 1 — Fork rbit 0.2.2 in-tree to drop reqwest and ring; announce HTTPS with rustls 0.23.46

`proposed` · `@templartorrent.decision.fork-rbit-for-native-gate/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "integration/rbit-adapter/**"`, `path "vendor/rbit/**"` · topic `rbit-fork`

Vendor rbit 0.2.2 into the repository as a path dependency applied through [patch.crates-io], make its reqwest dependency optional behind a Cargo feature that TemplarTorrent does not enable, and announce with an application-owned bounded HTTP/1.1 client that connects to the already-admitted tracker address. HTTPS announces use rustls 0.23.46, pinned, with default features off and only std, tls12 and aws_lc_rs enabled. That is the cryptography provider the 2026-10-14 rustls release enables by default. ring is not enabled. Certificate verification uses the webpki public roots and is not disabled. Redirects stay refused and the 64 KiB response cap stays.

**Context.** The strict native-source audit reported ring 0.17.14 through rbit -> reqwest (rustls-tls) -> rustls -> ring. The owner chose the fork on 2026-10-22 over accepting ring. On 2026-10-22 the owner then chose the recently updated rustls repository (stable release 0.23.46) for HTTPS trackers. That release's default provider is aws-lc-rs, which builds aws-lc (C, via cmake) rather than ring. rustls-rustcrypto remains the experimental provider the audit already rejected. Brotli certificate decompression stays off; 0.23.46's advisory GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv is about that disabled feature.

**Consequences.** The adapter still depends on the rbit API surface, and rbit upgrades require re-applying the feature gate. HTTP and HTTPS tracker announces are the application's responsibility. aws-lc-sys is now an accepted native dependency for tracker TLS only; cargo tree -i ring and -i reqwest stay empty, and the strict all-Rust claim does not cover aws-lc. WebSeed and UPnP from rbit stay unavailable.

## templartorrent.decision.http-download-manager

### Revision 1 — Extend the client into an HTTP(S) file download manager on the existing transport

`proposed` · `@templartorrent.decision.http-download-manager/1` · scope `path "DESIGN.md"`, `path "crates/templartorrent-core/src/bandwidth.rs"`, `path "integration/**"` · topic `http-downloads`

Add URL jobs for ordinary http:// and https:// files to the same application, queue, Add dialog, remove dialog and session store as torrents (DESIGN.md section 11). Downloads run over the application's rustls 0.23.46 transport with certificate name checks, a cap of 5 re-admitted redirects, refusal of non-http schemes and of private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, unique-local and metadata addresses unless --allow-local-urls or the matching setting is on. A 206 to a Range probe splits files of at least 1 MiB into 4 parallel parts by default and 8 at most, each charging its 64 KiB read buffer to the global payload budget and its bytes to the shared download token bucket; otherwise one connection. Resume needs a strong validator (quoted non-weak ETag, else Last-Modified at least 60 s older than Date) echoed unchanged by a 206 at the requested offset; a mismatch stops the job with a visible reason and keeps the partial file. A connection is dropped after 30 s without data and retried with bounded backoff; there is no total timeout. Bytes go to a temporary sibling, are synced, optionally checked against a user-supplied SHA-256, then renamed. Unknown sizes render as an em dash. Jobs persist as <key>.url records and are restored on launch.

**Context.** The user asked on 2026-11-03 to extend TemplarTorrent into a download manager for ordinary files, using https://github.com/ekremx25/linux-download-manager (registered as source ldm-readme-v0.3.0) only as a behaviour reference: its transfer rules, not its stack. Before this decision Command::Add accepted a magnet or a .torrent only; the HTTP code in announce.rs and portmap.rs had no Range requests, no file writer, no resume identity and no URL job. rbit's webseed module stays unwired; BEP 19 webseeds are a separate feature.

**Consequences.** DESIGN.md section 1 no longer defines a torrent-only product, but still rules out a webview, a second GUI, a media player, stream capture, content search, a browser extension in this tree and any background service after the window closes. Tauri, WebKit, yt-dlp, FFmpeg, HLS and tray-hide mode from the reference are not adopted. The adapter gains an http module and a sha2 dependency already present in the graph through rbit; the engine's download bucket becomes a shared handle so one limit governs peers and URL connections. URL jobs are admitted as their own pool of the Download jobs size. Proof is localhost fixtures only; Internet transfers stay opt-in. Browser link capture is reviewed in a repository markdown rather than implemented.
